hero.lead: A nation of 54.9 million between South and Southeast Asia, rich in forest, rivers and land, where on the 2019 data only one child in ten could read a simple text by the end of primary school.

capital.heading: Great natural wealth, waiting for the conditions to finance it.

record.text: General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025
UN appeal for 2026, for 4.9 million of the 16.2 million people in need; 43% received by 13 July 2026
ADB’s largest grant for the people of Myanmar, approved 17 June 2025 and delivered by UNDP, UNICEF and WFP

register.name: EU humanitarian aid for Myanmar, 2026
register.detail: Announced 30 January 2026 · Initial 2026 allocation · Part of €63 million for the Myanmar crisis and Rohingya refugees in neighbouring countries
register.note: More than €38.6 million for Myanmar itself; €23.4 million for Bangladesh
register.text: The European Union’s initial humanitarian allocation for 2026 for people affected by the crisis in Myanmar. It funds food assistance and emergency nutrition, shelter for displaced people, water and sanitation, health care and education in emergencies, which reach the food, shelter, water, health and education standards.

register.name: WFP plan for Myanmar, 2026
register.detail: Announced 11 December 2025 · 1.3 million people to be assisted · More than 12 million people projected to face acute hunger in 2026
register.note: WFP describes its Myanmar operation as massively underfunded
register.text: The World Food Programme’s budget for Myanmar in 2026, to assist 1.3 million people with food and nutrition support. It carries the food standard for the families furthest from it.

register.name: Myanmar Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
register.detail: Published 10 December 2025 · 16.2 million people in need · 4.9 million targeted · 2.6 million prioritised at $521 million · 43% received by 13 July 2026
register.note: 1.6 million people reached by 31 March 2026, a third of the target
register.text: The appeal of the United Nations and its partners for Myanmar in 2026, for 4.9 million of the more than 16 million people who need life-saving assistance and protection. It carries food, water, shelter, health care and learning in emergencies to the people furthest from the seven standards.

register.name: UNICEF Humanitarian Action for Children, Myanmar 2026
register.detail: 2026 appeal · 3.3 million people, including 2.6 million children · $95.4 million received by mid-2026, a gap of 64 per cent
register.note: 472,742 children reached with education, January to June 2026
register.text: UNICEF’s humanitarian appeal for Myanmar in 2026. It funds primary health care, nutrition, water and sanitation supplies and formal and non-formal learning for 667,000 children, which reach the health, food, water and education standards, the last of them furthest from reach.

register.name: Myanmar Earthquake: HNRP Flash Addendum 2025
register.detail: Published 11 April 2025, after the earthquakes of 28 March 2025 · 1.1 million people targeted · $209.6 million received (76.2%), on 10 February 2026
register.note: The response to earthquake needs continued into 2026
register.text: The United Nations appeal for the people hit by the earthquakes of March 2025, added to the humanitarian plan for 2025. It sought $275.2 million for 1.1 million people, and about three quarters was received; life-saving assistance after a disaster reaches the food, water, shelter and health standards.

register.name: DEC Myanmar Earthquake Appeal
register.detail: Launched 3 April 2025 · £28.0 million raised by February 2026, including £5 million of UK Aid Match · Phase 2 October 2025 to March 2027
register.note: 533,000 people reached in the first six months; £8.4 million spent in Phase 1
register.text: The appeal of the UK’s Disasters Emergency Committee charities for the people hit by the earthquakes of March 2025, given by the public and matched in part by the UK government. Its first phase delivered cash, shelter, water, food and health care; the second, to March 2027, puts livelihoods, cash, water and shelter first.

register.name: World Bank earthquake response through UN agencies
register.detail: Reported in the Myanmar Economic Monitor, December 2025 · Through UN agencies and public international organisations
register.note: World Bank support for basic services and livelihoods runs through UN agencies and the ICRC
register.text: World Bank funds allocated for the response to the earthquakes of March 2025, delivered through UN agencies and public international organisations. The source does not break the amount down by standard; the Bank describes its support in Myanmar as essential basic services and livelihood assistance.

register.name: Global Fund emergency funding for the earthquake response
register.detail: Announced 14 April 2025 · Emergency funding allocation · With partners in Myanmar, including local health organisations
register.note: Keeps HIV, TB and malaria care going after the earthquakes
register.text: An emergency allocation of the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria after the earthquakes of 28 March 2025. It buys antiretroviral drugs, TB medicines and malaria diagnostics and restores disrupted health services, which carries the health standard.
by: Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria

register.name: ADB grant for humanitarian relief and community resilience
register.detail: Approved 17 June 2025 · Asian Development Fund · Delivered by UNDP, UNICEF and WFP
register.note: ADB’s largest grant for the people of Myanmar; its regular operations have been on hold since 1 February 2021
register.text: An Asian Development Fund grant, delivered by three UN agencies, for food, water, emergency shelter and medical care, cash transfers, repairs to temporary learning spaces and teacher training, and farm roads, irrigation and water works. It reaches food, water, shelter, health, education and livelihood together.

register.name: ADB earthquake relief grant
register.detail: Announced 1 April 2025 · Asia Pacific Disaster Response Fund · Delivered by WFP
register.note: Food and multipurpose cash after the earthquakes of March 2025
register.text: A grant from ADB’s Asia Pacific Disaster Response Fund, delivered by the World Food Programme, for food supplies and multipurpose cash to buy drinking water, medical supplies and shelter. It reaches the food, water, health and shelter standards of the families hit.

register.name: Republic of Korea: REACH, second phase
register.detail: Announced 20 August 2026 · Through WFP · Relief food for 140,000 people · Nutrition support for 15,000 children under five
register.note: Internally displaced people and conflict-affected families first
register.text: A contribution of the Republic of Korea to the World Food Programme for the second phase of REACH, the joint Korea and WFP response in Myanmar. It delivers relief food and nutrition support for young children and for pregnant and breastfeeding women, which carries the food and health standards.

register.name: Australian development assistance to Myanmar, 2026–27
register.detail: Budget estimate · Total ODA A$123.6 million, of which bilateral A$46.1 million · A$124.8 million in 2025–26
register.note: Delivered through UN agencies, NGOs and civil society, with no direct funding to the Myanmar authorities
register.text: Australia’s estimated development assistance to Myanmar for 2026–27, delivered through UN agencies, multilateral and regional partners, NGOs and civil society organisations. It builds resilience through health, education and livelihoods and funds humanitarian aid for people displaced by conflict, which reaches the health, education and livelihood standards.

register.name: Sweden: Sida humanitarian allocation for Myanmar, 2026
register.detail: Humanitarian Crisis Analysis, 31 March 2026 · Initial allocation · ACF, ICRC, IRC, NRC, WFP and the Myanmar Humanitarian Fund
register.note: SEK 21 million of it goes to the pooled Myanmar Humanitarian Fund
register.text: Sweden’s humanitarian funding for Myanmar in 2026, through six partners including the pooled Myanmar Humanitarian Fund. It puts health, nutrition, food security, shelter and water, sanitation and hygiene first, with education and protection, which reach the health, food, shelter, water and education standards.

register.name: Republic of Korea: REACH, first phase
register.detail: Announced 5 September 2025 · Through WFP · Two months of food or cash for 300,000 people · Nutrition support for 24,000 pregnant and breastfeeding women and children
register.note: Conflict- and earthquake-affected areas, with a focus on hard-to-reach areas
register.text: A contribution of the Republic of Korea to the World Food Programme for REACH, emergency food and cash-for-food for families affected by conflict and the earthquakes, with nutrition support to prevent and treat malnutrition. It carries the food and health standards.

register.name: Global Innovation Fund grant to Proximity Designs
register.detail: Test and Transition grant · Provided 2024 for two years · 46,000 rice farmers targeted, 150,000 over three years
register.note: No-Burn Rice Farming: rice stubble decomposed instead of burned
register.text: A grant from the Global Innovation Fund to test and scale No-Burn Rice Farming, a low-cost method by which farmers decompose rice stubble with a bio-decomposer and nitrogen fertiliser instead of burning their fields. It serves the food and livelihood standards of smallholder rice farmers.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Teak and tropical forest across two fifths of the land.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: The Irrawaddy and its tributaries: more than 18,000 cubic metres of fresh water a person each year.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Half the power from water, with vast rivers still unharnessed.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: The Irrawaddy delta: rice for the nation and the region.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 24.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Proximity Designs
items.text: Helps smallholder farmers raise their productivity and incomes through innovative technologies and services; its affordable method lets rice farmers decompose crop residues in two weeks or less instead of burning them, for household gains of US$247 to US$301 a season.

items.name: MyFarmer Labs
items.text: Runs the MyFarmer App, a crowd-farming platform that connects individual investors with smallholder farmers who need capital and tracks each contract through to harvest; its pilot in southern Shan State financed 10 farmers with US$250 each.

items.name: Nae Thit Kyan Mar (New Day Health)
items.text: A social enterprise clinic in South Dagon Township, Yangon, that offers affordable prevention, diagnosis and treatment of diabetes, hypertension and other non-communicable diseases, with patients and donors sharing the cost; about 400 patients had enrolled by June 2024.

items.name: Early Dawn Microfinance
items.text: One of the five largest microfinance institutions in Myanmar, with more than US$90 million in assets, it lends to low-income micro-entrepreneurs in peri-urban and rural areas, and in 2025 FMO provided the equivalent of €10 million in local currency for its microloans to women.

items.name: BRAC Myanmar Microfinance Company Limited
items.text: Offers loans for women’s microenterprises, farming and small enterprises, and savings, to people living in poverty, and reports 124,846 borrowers and 265,597 savers, 99% of its clients women.

coverage.gap_text: Of children in Myanmar cannot read a simple text by the end of primary school, on 2019 data.

guarantees.name: Energy

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 10.5% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school; 2019, dated

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$4.20 a day; 29.1% live below it, dated
